units.function: Resolves whether an authenticated Agent run is a persisted task-watchdog execution and restricts its Issue mutations to the watched non-watchdog subtree or the reusable watchdog Issue.
units.dependencyDirection: The scope resolver directly reads Heartbeat runs, Issue watchdogs and parent-linked Issues through Drizzle. HTTP routes consume the returned tagged scope; the module has no dependency on those routes.
units.keyDataModels: Agent run actor, HeartbeatRun contextSnapshot.taskWatchdog, active IssueWatchdog, watched Issue, watchdog Issue and a maximum-100-level parent ancestry traversal.
units.lifecycle: Validate actor/run ownership and tenant; recover watched Issue and stop fingerprint from persisted run context; require a matching active watchdog; for each mutation walk parents inside the company, reject cycles, missing rows, watchdog-origin ancestors and out-of-subtree targets.
units.testAssessment: The route suite covers allowed watched descendants, the reusable watchdog Issue, denied watchdog descendants, unrelated targets, nested watchdog configuration and cross-scope interaction resolution. There is no isolated test for malformed contexts, 100-level boundary behavior, cyclic ancestry, deleted/reparented trees, concurrent watchdog disable or TOCTOU between scope check and mutation.
units.designRationale: Treat prompt-described capabilities as insufficient and reconstruct mutation authority from persisted run, watchdog and Issue state.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs every Connector execution to carry a durable, narrow authority grant that is revalidated against current work, responsibility, approval and data contracts before side effects.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the persisted-scope reconstruction, tenant binding, subtree exclusion and pre-mutation revalidation. Replace route-specific ancestry checks with a versioned CapabilityGrant/ActionAuthorization port bound to run, work, responsible human, permission/data digests and expiry/fencing version.
units.responsibilityConflict: The grant is derived from an Agent-owned watchdog and stop fingerprint only. It permits status changes, reassignment and child creation without an accountable-human authority record, and it does not bind tool/data scope or a high-risk approval digest.

units.function: Task-subtree watchdog domain/application service: classifies live, first-run-pending, already-reviewed or stopped trees; persists watchdog configuration and snapshots; creates/reuses review Issues; schedules idempotent Agent wakes; records activities; and revalidates stopped fingerprints before mutations.
units.dependencyDirection: Pure classification and fingerprint helpers share one 1,815-line module with Drizzle queries, Issue creation/comments, Agent invokability, activity logging and wake scheduling. It depends on many Paperclip tables and Issue/Heartbeat conventions, so it is not a portable service boundary.
units.keyDataModels: IssueWatchdog and summary; v2 stop snapshot with material leaves and pending waits; live Run/Wakeup paths; Issue blockers/interactions/approvals; reusable task_watchdog Issue; reviewed and observed fingerprints; Agent wake capability description.
units.lifecycle: Upsert one watchdog per company/Issue; recursively collect the visible non-watchdog subtree; classify live paths, first-run races and stopped material state; hash a canonical snapshot; suppress identical or shrink-only reviewed states; create/reopen one review Issue; log and wake the watchdog Agent with scoped capabilities; mark a completed review fingerprint; reconcile periodically or on ancestor mutation; re-evaluate the exact fingerprint before allowing a watchdog mutation.
units.testAssessment: Pure classifier and embedded-Postgres scheduler/route suites cover metadata-stable hashes, changed material state, shrink-only suppression, JSON key order, live paths, queued wakes, create races, nested watchdog exclusion, reusable review Issues, stale in_review, old-versus-new fingerprints, wait projection, atomic setup, concurrent upsert, tenant isolation and scoped mutations. Missing evidence includes graph cycles/depth truncation, two scheduler processes racing to comment/wake, crash points across Issue/comment/watchdog/activity/wake writes, outbox delivery, malicious JSON/context, high-volume query plans, human approval authority and data-policy revalidation.
units.designRationale: Detect a whole task tree that has no live execution path without generating duplicate escalation noise, and give a dedicated Agent enough constrained context to verify or restore the work.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs a responsibility-aware Intervention Policy that detects stalled work graphs, distinguishes legitimate waits, produces one durable incident per material state and routes it to the correct accountable human/Agent Boss with evidence.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the pure material-state classifier, versioned canonical fingerprint, reviewed-snapshot shrink rule, first-run race guard, reusable incident and exact pre-action revalidation. Split Company OS ownership into WorkLivenessPolicy, InterventionCase aggregate, AuthorizationGrant and durable outbox; route high-risk decisions to accountable humans and treat approval/data waits as typed contracts.
units.responsibilityConflict: A system process wakes a watchdog Agent and grants reassignment/status/child-creation operations through context JSON. Pending approvals are evidence in a stop snapshot, not authority constraints. Sequential writes can leave the review Issue, fingerprint, activity and wake inconsistent, and the review may be marked complete from mutable Issue disposition without a signed human receipt.

units.function: Pure executable specification for task-subtree liveness, material stop fingerprints, reviewed-state suppression and the first-run race window.
units.dependencyDirection: Imports only the exported classifier/type from task-watchdogs and supplies in-memory Issue/path/wait fixtures.
units.keyDataModels: Classifier Issue tree, live run/wake paths, blocker and wait IDs, v2 material stop snapshot, reviewed fingerprint/snapshot and first-run timing inputs.
units.lifecycle: Build tree snapshots; classify live/stopped/pending/already-reviewed; compare fingerprints after metadata, leaf, assignee, blocker and wait changes; exclude watchdog-origin subtrees.
units.testAssessment: Fifteen named tests plus five material-change table cases give strong deterministic policy coverage. Gaps include cycles, depth/size bounds, duplicate IDs, invalid dates, tenant-mixed parents, ordering/property tests, human waits and approval/data-contract semantics.
units.designRationale: Keep noise-suppression and race-handling semantics independent of database orchestration.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs pure, replayable liveness and intervention policy tests with stable versioned outputs.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the table-driven material-change and race-window scenarios; add property tests, responsibility and authorization waits, and explicit policy-version migration fixtures.
units.responsibilityConflict: The classifier treats pending approvals as fingerprint material but does not decide which human owns the wait or whether an Agent may act around it.

units.function: Embedded-Postgres integration specification for watchdog reconciliation, reusable review Issues, wake idempotency/context, reviewed snapshots, stale review recovery and mutation-fingerprint revalidation.
units.dependencyDirection: Invokes taskWatchdogService against real Paperclip schema and captures a fake wake adapter, spanning Issues, Runs, Wake requests, Approvals, Interactions, Documents, Work Products, comments and activity logs.
units.keyDataModels: Company, Agent, Issue tree, IssueWatchdog, HeartbeatRun, AgentWakeupRequest, pending approval/interaction, evidence timestamps, stop snapshots and activity records.
units.lifecycle: Seed watchdogs and tree state; reconcile; inspect created/reopened review Issue, snapshots, comments and wake context; change live/material/review state; reconcile again; verify suppression, re-trigger or stale-scope denial.
units.testAssessment: Eighteen integration cases cover initial trigger, duplicate suppression, stale review, Run/Wakeup live paths, nested exclusion, ancestor reconciliation, reviewed snapshot reuse and JSON round-trip, old/new fingerprint ordering, evidence-only changes, wait payloads, create-race, true idle work and recursion prevention. It does not inject failures between sequential writes, run concurrent reconcilers, verify durable wake uniqueness in the database, test large/deep trees or assert human authority and Connector evidence receipts.
units.designRationale: Protect the cross-table invariants that the pure classifier alone cannot prove.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs intervention compatibility tests spanning event replay, incident projection, authorization, notification and recovery across managed and local profiles.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE the scenario catalog but implement against Company OS public ports/events and transactional outbox, including crash matrices and multi-node races.
units.responsibilityConflict: The scheduler proves an Agent wake, not accountable-human acknowledgement or approval; its success criteria omit immutable responsibility and data authorization receipts.

units.function: HTTP/API integration suite for watchdog CRUD, atomic Issue creation, Agent invokability, tenant isolation and persisted mutation scope enforcement.
units.dependencyDirection: Assembles Express Issue routes with embedded PostgreSQL, mocked execution adapter and real Heartbeat/task-watchdog services; it therefore validates public route behavior and several application internals together.
units.keyDataModels: Cloud user membership/default grants, Agent, Issue/relations, IssueWatchdog, Heartbeat run, Agent runtime state, activity/event rows and watchdog-discovered product-bug provenance.
units.lifecycle: Create/update/read/list/disable watchdogs; concurrently upsert; atomically create Issue plus watchdog; reject premature first-run review; execute an Agent watchdog run; allow only scoped tree mutations; route product bugs outside the watched tree with evidence; deny foreign tenants and non-invokable Agents.
units.testAssessment: Nine named cases plus three Agent-status cases cover important authorization and tenant behavior, including uniform cross-tenant 404 and twelve concurrent upserts. Assertions depend on English error strings and Paperclip route shapes. Missing cases include stable error codes, human role matrix beyond owner, revoked membership during a run, exact approval/data scope, TOCTOU transactions, malformed watchdog discovery evidence and cross-node concurrency.
units.designRationale: Ensure an Agent's watchdog context cannot become a general-purpose mutation privilege and preserve source-tree cleanliness for discovered product bugs.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs stable API contracts that expose intervention setup while preventing an execution Connector from escaping its responsibility and data scope.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the uniform tenant-not-found response, database-backed authority reconstruction, concurrent upsert and atomic setup cases. Use structured error codes, capability receipts and accountable-human grants in Company OS public API tests.
units.responsibilityConflict: A cloud owner configures the watchdog, but subsequent Agent mutation authority is not bound to that human's continuing responsibility or an explicit approval. English strings are used as test contracts.
